title: Are Berlin’s Attractions Worth It? - Quick Summary
items: **Berlin's five branded indoor attractions are now three.** Sea Life Berlin and Little BIG City both closed for good in December 2024. Madame Tussauds, the Berlin Dungeon and LEGOLAND Discovery Centre are the survivors.
**Whether they are worth it depends on your group, not on the venue.** For €20 to €30 a head, the right visitor has a great afternoon and the wrong one feels taxed.
**Madame Tussauds (Unter den Linden 74) is a teen and photo stop.** About €22 online versus €29.50 at the door, roughly an hour. Fun for selfies, thin as the memory of a Berlin trip.

**The Berlin Dungeon near Alexanderplatz is an 80-minute live-actor scare show performed largely in German.** From €18 online, best for teens about 10 and up; non-German speakers miss most of the script.

**LEGOLAND Discovery Centre (Sony Center, Potsdamer Platz) is only for young kids, about 3 to 10.** €19.50 online, two to three hours, and adults get in only with a child. A strong rainy-day pick for the right family.
**Always book online, and treat these as backup, not the plan.** For the same money, a real view, a museum or a walking tour shows you far more of Berlin.
